q: The decode-forward (DF) strategy for the relay channel achieves rates up to min(I(X;Y_R|X_R), I(X,X_R;Y)). A key limitation is:
opts: The relay must know the channel
The relay must fully decode the source message, which requires I(X;Y_R) ≥ R (bottleneck at weak relay-destination link)
exp: DF's bottleneck: the relay must reliably decode the source message, requiring R ≤ I(X;Y_R). If the source-relay link is weak, DF may not be better than direct transmission. Compress-forward (CF) does not require decoding and can outperform DF when the relay-destination link is strong.
